h: Adam, Eve and a peek at the Mersey
p: Walk into the cobbled courtyard at the heart of the house and you will meet two ancient yew trees, known as Adam and Eve. They have stood here for centuries and give the courtyard a slightly magical feel, especially on a misty morning.

Like many houses of its era, Speke Hall has hidden secrets. It was home to a Catholic family in Tudor times, and it has a priest hole and a little spyhole, said to have been used for eavesdropping on visitors at the front door. Kids love hunting for these and trying to imagine life when hiding in the walls might be a matter of life and death.

Head out onto the Bund, a raised bank in the grounds, for views across the Mersey estuary towards the Wirral and, on a clear day, the hills of North Wales. It is surprising to find such a peaceful view so close to a busy airport.
Allow at least half a day to enjoy the house, gardens and woodland. Bring wellies if it has been raining, as the woods can be muddy.

Back in the city, the Royal Albert Dock is home to Tate Liverpool, the Merseyside Maritime Museum and The Beatles Story, and the Museum of Liverpool sits on the waterfront nearby. It is easy to round off a Tudor morning with a proper Scouse afternoon.
The grounds also make a fine picnic spot on a sunny day, with plenty of lawn to spread out on while the kids explore.
